title: Add csnotes study command for interactive course review
description:
Adds 'csnotes study --course {name}' for interactive AI-assisted exam prep.

## Use case

Student wants to talk to Claude about course material to cement understanding and get quizzed — not to synthesize new atomic notes. The AI needs full context of what has been covered (notes, recordings, sources, existing atomics) but produces no vault changes.

## What this is NOT

Not a synthesis pass. No ops report, no commit loop. The workspace is read-only context for a freeform conversation.

## Design

- New top-level command: csnotes study --course {name}
- Builds a CourseScope workspace (depends on L52) with all processed session inputs + course-filtered sources + existing synthetic notes
- Launches AI without a skill schema — open-ended prompt: 'here is what this student has been studying, help them review'
- No SessionEntry written to manifest; optionally write a lightweight study log entry (date, course, run_id) for reference
- Backend: probably same AI backend as process, but no structured output expected

## Open questions

- Which backends make sense? (Claude interactive terminal session vs agy)
- Should the workspace be assembled to disk the same way as process, or streamed differently?
- Study log: worth tracking in manifest or overkill?

## Depends on

L52 (course-scoped workspace assembly)
